scope.purpose: Small agent-reviewed multilingual search relevance probe: does the native web search path return on-topic entities for specific en/zh/es queries?

relevance_scale.relevant: result is the expected entity/source or a direct authoritative page for the requested topic
relevance_scale.partially_relevant: right topic family but not the requested entity/language/source (e.g. English page for a Chinese query, secondary tutorial)
relevance_scale.not_relevant: different topic, different library, or content-free aggregator

gaps: All 9 hits came back with an empty snippet on this path (engine jina_duckduckgo returns title+URL only). Relevance review therefore rests on titles/URLs plus the three native reads, not on returned snippets.

ddg_lite and ddg_html were attempted before jina_duckduckgo on all three queries and produced no hits; one engine served every query, so results are engine-correlated and no independent second backend was exercised.
No public optional backend fallback was needed: every query returned 3 hits on the first search call. Fallback remains untested for these queries.

Language targeting is partial, not absent: rank 1 was the requested-language page only for the English query. For zh and es the requested-language official page appeared at rank 2 behind a third-party tutorial (zh) and an English page (es).
Only the top 3 hits per query were inspected. Expected entities outside the top 3 (PEP 484, mypy zh, es.wikipedia) are unverified — absence from top 3 is not evidence of absence.
The zh read was truncated at the extractor readable-text cap (20,004 chars); the page continues upstream.
No recall, completeness, latency, or cross-tool comparison was measured. This is a 3-query relevance probe whose verdicts are one agent's reading of titles, URLs, and read text.
Titles carry upstream version labels (Python 3.15.2, Requests 2.34.2) that were not re-verified against the live pages beyond the three reads.

summary.note: 5/9 hits were the expected entity/source; 4/9 were the right topic but the wrong source or language. No not-relevant or duplicate hits. No superiority, parity, or completeness claim is made.
